_metadata.description: Regulatory reference data for food additives. Sources: FSSAI, EFSA, Codex Alimentarius, FDA, IARC.
_metadata.disclaimer: Regulatory approval indicates a substance is permitted at specified levels. It does not imply the substance is harmless at all doses or beneficial for all individuals. This data is for educational reference only.
_metadata.verification_status: Partial — entries marked verified:true have been cross-checked against primary sources. Others are preliminary.

INS 100.name: Curcumin
INS 100.fssai_status: Permitted — used in specified food categories
INS 100.applicable_conditions: Permitted in processed foods at levels specified per food category. Maximum levels vary by category (e.g. 200 mg/kg in some dairy products).
INS 100.regulatory_notes: Natural pigment from turmeric. No significant safety concerns at normal food use levels.

INS 102.name: Tartrazine
INS 102.fssai_status: Permitted with conditions — maximum use levels specified per food category
INS 102.codex_status: Listed in GSFA with specific maximum levels
INS 102.fda_status: Permitted with certification requirement (FD&C Yellow No. 5)
INS 102.applicable_conditions: EU requires 'may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children' warning label. Maximum 100 mg/kg in non-alcoholic flavoured drinks (Codex). FDA requires label declaration by name.
INS 102.regulatory_notes: One of the Southampton 6 dyes. EFSA (2009) concluded no evidence of hyperactivity at ADI levels but noted sensitivity in some individuals.

INS 110.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
INS 110.efsa_adi: 0–1 mg/kg bw/day (EFSA 2014, significantly reduced from 4 mg/kg bw/day)
INS 110.applicable_conditions: EU hyperactivity warning label required. EFSA 2014 substantially reduced ADI. Maximum levels vary by food category.
INS 110.regulatory_notes: Southampton 6 dye. EFSA 2014 reduced ADI substantially. EU hyperactivity warning label required.

INS 129.name: Allura Red AC
INS 129.applicable_conditions: EU hyperactivity warning label required. EFSA 2022 re-evaluation reduced ADI from 7 to 0.5 mg/kg bw/day — significant change from prior assessment.
INS 129.regulatory_notes: Southampton 6 dye. EFSA 2022 re-evaluation raised concerns at typical intake levels for children.

INS 200.name: Sorbic Acid
INS 200.applicable_conditions: Group ADI applies to all sorbates combined (INS 200, 201, 202, 203). Permitted in baked goods, dairy, beverages, processed fruits and vegetables at specified maximum levels.
INS 200.regulatory_notes: Wide use as preservative in baked goods, dairy, beverages. Low toxicity at permitted levels.

INS 202.name: Potassium Sorbate
INS 202.efsa_adi: 0–3 mg/kg bw/day (group ADI with sorbic acid)
INS 202.applicable_conditions: Group ADI shared with sorbic acid (INS 200) and other sorbate salts. Combined intake from all sources must remain within group ADI.
INS 202.regulatory_notes: Common preservative. Group ADI applies to all sorbates combined.

INS 210.name: Benzoic Acid
INS 210.applicable_conditions: Group ADI includes benzoic acid and benzoate salts (INS 210–213). Can combine with ascorbic acid (vitamin C) to form benzene — use in combination with ascorbic acid requires care.
INS 210.regulatory_notes: Hyperactivity concern when combined with certain artificial colors (Southampton study). EFSA 2016 group ADI.

INS 211.name: Sodium Benzoate
INS 211.efsa_adi: 0–5 mg/kg bw/day (group with benzoic acid, EFSA 2016)
INS 211.applicable_conditions: Should not be used in combination with ascorbic acid (vitamin C) in beverages due to risk of benzene formation. Group ADI applies. EU requires hyperactivity warning if combined with Southampton 6 colors.
INS 211.regulatory_notes: Can react with ascorbic acid (vitamin C) to form benzene (a carcinogen) in beverages. EFSA noted hyperactivity link when combined with artificial colors.

INS 220.name: Sulphur Dioxide
INS 220.authority: EFSA / FSSAI / EU Regulation / Codex Alimentarius
INS 220.applicable_conditions: Mandatory allergen declaration required in India above threshold (10 mg/kg). EU Annex II allergen — must be declared on label at any level. Group ADI applies to all sulphites (INS 220–228).
INS 220.regulatory_notes: EU allergen list (Annex II Regulation 1169/2011). Can trigger asthma and allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

INS 250.name: Sodium Nitrite
INS 250.authority: EFSA / FSSAI / FDA / IARC / Codex Alimentarius
INS 250.fssai_status: Permitted in meat products only — strict maximum levels apply
INS 250.efsa_adi: No established ADI (EFSA 2017) — use should be minimised
INS 250.codex_status: Listed for processed meat only with strict limits
INS 250.applicable_conditions: Restricted to cured and processed meat products only. Not permitted in poultry or fish in many jurisdictions. FSSAI maximum: 125 mg/kg in cured meat. Essential function: prevents Clostridium botulinum growth in cured meats.
INS 250.regulatory_notes: IARC classified processed meat (containing nitrite) as Group 1 carcinogen (2015). EFSA (2017): current dietary exposure may be of concern. Endogenous nitrosamine formation linked to colorectal cancer risk.

INS 300.name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
INS 300.efsa_adi: Not specified (acceptable for normal food use)
INS 300.applicable_conditions: No specific maximum level for general use — quantum satis (QS) principle applies in most categories. Avoid combination with sodium benzoate in acidic beverages (benzene formation risk).
INS 300.regulatory_notes: Natural antioxidant. No safety concerns at normal food use levels. Can react with sodium benzoate to form benzene — avoid combination in beverages.

INS 320.name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole (BHA)
INS 320.authority: EFSA / FSSAI / FDA / IARC / Codex Alimentarius
INS 320.applicable_conditions: Maximum 200 mg/kg in fats and oils (FSSAI). Often used in combination with BHT — combined maximum applies. Not permitted in infant foods.
INS 320.regulatory_notes: IARC Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans) based on animal studies. Some countries restrict use.

INS 321.name: Butylated Hydroxytoluene (BHT)
INS 321.applicable_conditions: Maximum 200 mg/kg in fats and oils (FSSAI). Often combined with BHA. Not permitted in infant foods. Some jurisdictions (e.g. Japan) restrict use in certain categories.
INS 321.regulatory_notes: Potential endocrine disruption concern in animal studies. Lower ADI than BHA. Some jurisdictions restrict or ban.

INS 330.name: Citric Acid
INS 330.applicable_conditions: Quantum satis (QS) — no fixed maximum for most food categories. Naturally present in citrus fruits. Wide use as acidity regulator and antioxidant synergist.
INS 330.regulatory_notes: Naturally occurring in citrus fruits. Widely used acidity regulator. No safety concerns at normal use levels.

INS 407.name: Carrageenan
INS 407.applicable_conditions: Food-grade (undegraded) carrageenan permitted. Degraded carrageenan (poligeenan) is NOT permitted in food. EU Regulation 2016/127 restricts use in infant formula and follow-on formula.
INS 407.regulatory_notes: Derived from red seaweed. Ongoing debate about gastrointestinal effects. EFSA recommending re-evaluation.

INS 471.name: Mono and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
INS 471.applicable_conditions: Quantum satis (QS) for most applications. Used as emulsifier in bakery products, margarines, ice cream, and beverages. No restriction on type of fatty acids specified (may include trans fats depending on source).
INS 471.regulatory_notes: Common emulsifier. No significant safety concerns at normal use levels.

INS 621.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
INS 621.efsa_adi: Not specified — safe at normal dietary exposure (EFSA 2017)
INS 621.applicable_conditions: No specific maximum for most applications (QS). EFSA (2017) recommended an ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day for the group of glutamates (INS 620–625). Contributes to overall dietary sodium intake.
INS 621.regulatory_notes: EFSA (2017) concluded safe at normal use levels. 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' not substantiated in controlled studies. High-dose sensitivity reported in some individuals.

INS 950.name: Acesulfame Potassium (Ace-K)
INS 950.applicable_conditions: Maximum levels vary by food category (e.g. 350 mg/L in non-alcoholic flavoured drinks per Codex). Often used in combination with other sweeteners for taste synergy.
INS 950.regulatory_notes: EFSA (2000) ADI. Under ongoing monitoring. Some animal studies suggest potential metabolic effects at high doses — not established in humans at normal dietary levels.
source_refs: EFSA SCF (2000) Reports of the Scientific Committee for Food

INS 951.name: Aspartame
INS 951.authority: EFSA / FSSAI / FDA / IARC / JECFA / Codex Alimentarius
INS 951.efsa_adi: 0–40 mg/kg bw/day (EFSA 2013 — maintained after full re-evaluation)
INS 951.applicable_conditions: Mandatory PKU warning: 'Contains a source of phenylalanine' required on all products. IARC classified as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic) in 2023. JECFA and EFSA maintained the ADI at 40 mg/kg bw/day. Not recommended for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU).
INS 951.regulatory_notes: IARC classified as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic) in July 2023 based on limited evidence. JECFA (2023) maintained ADI, concluding evidence insufficient to revise. Regulatory authorities (EFSA, FDA, FSSAI) consider safe within ADI.

INS 955.name: Sucralose
INS 955.efsa_adi: 0–15 mg/kg bw/day (EFSA 2017, reduced from earlier value)
INS 955.applicable_conditions: Maximum levels vary by product category. EFSA 2017 revised ADI downward from previous assessments. Often combined with other sweeteners. Some heat stability limitations at high temperatures.
INS 955.regulatory_notes: EFSA 2017 revised ADI downward. Some studies suggest gut microbiome effects at high doses — not established at normal dietary levels.

INS 150D.name: Caramel IV (Sulphite Ammonia Caramel)
INS 150D.authority: EFSA / FSSAI / FDA / California OEHHA / Codex Alimentarius
INS 150D.fda_status: Permitted — California Prop 65 warning required above 29μg/day 4-MEI
INS 150D.applicable_conditions: Group ADI for caramel colours. California Proposition 65: products contributing >29 μg/day of 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) require cancer warning. Major use in cola beverages, soy sauce, beer.
INS 150D.regulatory_notes: Contains 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) as a processing contaminant. California OEHHA listed 4-MEI as a known carcinogen (Prop 65). EFSA (2011) concluded no public health concern within ADI.
